In Nyaya logic, a reason (hetu) that is always found with the **absence** of the thing to be proved is the **viruddha** (contradictory) hetvabhasa: it proves the opposite of what is claimed.

"Sound is eternal because it is produced": whatever is produced is non-eternal, so being produced goes with the absence of eternality. This is the standard example of viruddha.

The others are different fallacies: "the hill has fire because it is knowable" is savyabhichara/sadharana (the reason is too wide), "sound is eternal because it is audible" is asadharana (the reason is too narrow), and "sound is a quality because it is visible" is asiddha (sound is not visible at all).
